root_idea.summary: The root is oriented toward a small amount or shortfall, especially a deficiency in what is measured.
root_idea.development: From the notion of slightness or deficiency, the lexicon develops related senses involving the brim or upper edge of a vessel, and hence being near, raised to a level, or brought within reach. Some further usages, such as cunning and attainment, are reported as divergent developments.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular active-participle citation form مُطَفِّفٌ; the Quran occurrence itself is plural.

senses.definition: One who gives short measure or short weight, defrauding the other party by making what is measured out deficient.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is plural مُطَفِّفِينَ. The usage concerns cheating in measure or weight by withholding part of what is due, including deficiency in the fulfillment or receipt of a measured amount.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become near, within reach, or attainable; of something, to rise into view and become available.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a thing approaching another thing, or of something becoming accessible or appearing ready to be taken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become little in quantity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general quantitative usage, distinct from the specialized act of short-measuring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pass by hastening or going quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported verbal usage describing rapid passage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bind all the legs of a she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with the she-camel as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To raise something or someone, make it level with a place, or mount upon a wall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes raising by the leg, foot, arm, or hand and ascending to a higher place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make defective or deficient.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broad Form II usage; its specialized application to short measure and weight is represented separately under the Quranic form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stint or impoverish one's household, acting niggardly in expenditure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application to expenditure on dependants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give a person less than he had taken from him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transaction-related construction expressing a deficient return.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take what lies upon or above the top of a vessel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A vessel-related construction involving the amount at the upper edge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make full or complete.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported contrary signification of the Form II verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the sun, to draw near to setting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source reports a possible transcription or form variant; the usage is retained as a cautious Classical meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a bird, to expand its wings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used specifically of a bird spreading or expanding its wings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse, to leap with its rider.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional equestrian usage describing a horse's leap carrying someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have knowledge of an affair or of a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with an affair or person as the object of knowledge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek to deceive someone, sometimes while knowing or observing him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported interpersonal usage involving an intention to outwit or deceive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To look upon something from above, see it, or obtain knowledge of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَلَى and related to looking over, overlooking, or becoming aware of something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gain possession of another person's property and take it away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is explicitly described as another person's property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reach or strike someone or something with a stone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction أَطَفَّ عَلَيْهِ بِحَجَرٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to cast or bring forth an imperfectly formed young one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the birth of incompletely developed offspring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put or bring something near.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of bringing an object into proximity, including bringing a razor near the nose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give someone power over a thing or place it within his reach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative construction expressing enablement or access.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hold a sword toward someone and strike him with it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A weapon-related construction combining presentation of the sword with striking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make the contents of a measure reach its uppermost part.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of filling a measure to the top; an alternative report says it can mean taking what lies above the measure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take what lies upon or above a measure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported alternative to the filling interpretation in the measure-related construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel's hump, to rise or become high.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used specifically of the camel's hump.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For what one wants to become prepared and easy to attain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a desired matter becoming accessible or ready.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become lax or weak in the hands of an adversary.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reduplicated-form usage describing loss of strength or resistance before an opponent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The side, bank, or shore of something; especially an elevated or bordering part of a river or land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also applied geographically to land overlooking a cultivated region.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The exterior court or yard of a house.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal spatial usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The amount reaching, rising above, nearly reaching, or slightly falling short of the brim of a measure or vessel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexicon reports variant interpretations concerning the quantity at the vessel's upper edge. It is also used figuratively in a comparison for near equality accompanied by slight deficiency.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The blackness of night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal time-related usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Small or scant in quantity; incomplete.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a thing that is slight in amount or deficient in completion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Low, base, vile, mean, paltry, or contemptible.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An evaluative adjectival usage, distinct from the quantitative sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The quantity above a measure, the amount falling short of filling a vessel, or a small quantity remaining in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also denotes the uppermost part of the vessel; the source reports variant interpretations concerning whether the amount is above or below the brim.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse, light, brisk, or quick.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet applied to a horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a vessel, full to its uppermost parts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a vessel whose contents have reached the top.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The strip between mountains and plains, or what surrounds a garden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A spatial noun for an intervening or surrounding boundary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The flank or soft, quivering flesh at the side of the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the soft parts of the belly, the extremities of the side adjoining the ribs, and the soft part of the liver.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The extremities of trees or the soft, tender, succulent parts of plants and herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May refer to the leaves of branches.

cautions: The sole QAC occurrence is the plural مُطَفِّفِينَ; the public headword is normalized to the singular citation form مُطَفِّفٌ.
The reported full-or-complete readings for Form II and Form IV are Classical usages and are not part of the Quranic sense.
The Form II sunset usage is retained with caution because the lexical source itself notes a possible transcription or form variant.
The Lane Quran reference associated with مُطَفِّفٌ is historical citation evidence; the modern example location supplied here is independently identified by QAC.
